name: KEMET-t521
title: T52X/T530 KO-CAP polymer electrolytic tantalum chip capacitors (T520, T521, T523, T525, T527, T529, T530, TF08)
summary: A family of surface-mount polymer tantalum chip capacitors, series T520, T521, T523, T525, T527, T529, T530 and TF08, spanning 0.68 to 1,500 µF and 2 to 75 V in EIA cases from 2012 to 7360. The conductive polymer cathode gives ESR as low as 4 mΩ, capacitance that holds up with temperature, bias and frequency, no ageing and high ripple current ratings. Depending on the part the top operating temperature is 85, 105 or 125°C. T521, the high-voltage line, is made for 12 V to 48 V rails; T521X336M050ATE050, for instance, is 33 µF, 50 V, 50 mΩ, 2.83 A rms ripple at 45°C and 100 kHz, in the 7343-43 X case.

operation.text: A surface-mount solid electrolytic tantalum capacitor with a conductive polymer cathode. The polymer gives a low ESR (down to 4 mΩ in the family) and keeps more of the capacitance at high frequency. The part shows no ageing effects, has a very long operating life compared with liquid-electrolyte capacitors and handles large ripple currents. Every part is given an accelerated steady-state ageing step and a surge current test before shipment.

T520 is the general range up to 10 V class rails; T521 covers 12 V to 48 V rails with ratings to 75 V, 105°C or 125°C classes and low leakage; T523 has its terminals only on the bottom face for low ESL; T525 and T530 are rated to 125°C, T530 being the high-capacitance, lowest-ESR line; T527, T529 and TF08 are thin or small cases (T529 on a substrate terminal, TF08 0.8 mm high). T520 and T525 parts for 12 V to 48 V rails are no longer recommended for new designs, and T521 replaces them.

A sintered tantalum anode carries a Ta2O5 dielectric, then a polymer layer, a carbon layer and a silver paint layer. A tantalum wire welded to the leadframe forms the anode (+) terminal; silver adhesive joins the cathode body to the cathode (−) leadframe. The body is moulded epoxy with a stripe and bevel at the anode end. T523, T527 and T529 add a spacer; T529 uses a substrate in place of a leadframe.

Rated voltage UR may be applied continuously up to the rated temperature TR. Above TR, up to the category temperature TC, the continuous limit is the category voltage UC. For parts rated 105°C with a 125°C category, UC is about two thirds of UR (for example 33.5 V for a 50 V part).

The average failure rate is 0.5 % per 1,000 hours at UC and TC; qualification runs for 1,000 or 2,000 hours depending on the part. Life lengthens as voltage and temperature drop below UC and TC; with UA below 0.9 UC and TA below 85°C the expected life is typically more than 10 years. The acceleration equations give an estimate.

The polymer capacitor has no wear-out mechanism within its ratings and may run at full rated voltage, but KEMET advises a steady-state voltage derating for demonstrated long-term reliability. Each part number has a derating category (Table 1) whose chart gives the recommended application voltage as a percentage of rated voltage against temperature.

The peak of the AC ripple plus any DC bias must stay at or below the rated voltage, and the negative peak with the bias must stay within the reverse voltage limit. Allowed ripple follows from the case's maximum power dissipation and the ESR; Table 1 gives the rms limit for each part at 45°C and 100 kHz, scaled down at higher temperature by the series multiplier.
Surge voltage is the highest peak that may be applied. It is not for repeated charge and discharge in normal operation and is not part of the working voltage.
The part is polarised and can be destroyed by reverse connection. Short transient reversal is tolerated up to 15% of rated voltage at 25°C, falling to 1% at 125°C.

Wave (single or dual), convection, IR and vapour-phase reflow are all usable, with preheating to limit thermal stress; the reflow profile follows J-STD-020D and three passes are allowed. The X case (4.3 mm tall) can be wave soldered but needs care. Hand soldering should heat the pad, not the moulded body, and the iron is removed as soon as the solder flows; wiping the chip edges or heating the top is to be avoided.
Pure tin terminations (standard or non-magnetic) and Ni-Pd-Au terminations make the part RoHS compliant; the part is halogen-free; epoxy rated UL94 V-0 except in the T529 series.

Larger cases (T520/T521/T523/T525/T530) carry a KO polarity band at the anode end, the three-digit picofarad code, the rated voltage, the KEMET K and a three-digit date code. Small cases carry a polarity band, a one-letter date code and a voltage-plus-capacitance code; 125°C T527 parts add an NH ID code.
